title: Streaming artifact annotations: span linkage and scrub policy
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: provide deterministic mappings from incremental streamed output artifacts to tracing spans and telemetry while ensuring no sensitive content is emitted into logs. This ticket defines the artifact annotation model, span-linking contract, metric names, and a scrub-first logging policy for streamed chunks. It also describes compatibility mappings for older clients that only know chunk_id semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Every streamed chunk emitted by the runtime includes an artifact_id and a trace link header when tracing is enabled
Per-chunk metrics (latency, tokens_generated, stall_count) emitted to prometheus/kafka with consistent labels: artifact_id, model, route, tenant
Logging pipeline drops or tokenizes PII per redaction policy before any chunk content is written to logs or traces
Legacy clients that expect chunk_id continue to be served with a stable chunk_id -> artifact_id mapping for 30 days
End-to-end tests covering span linkage, metrics ingestion, and redaction pass in CI and in a staging canary
proposal_summary: Introduce an immutable artifact_id for each logical output fragment. Instrument the streaming runtime to attach artifact_id and trace_link (trace_id/span_id) to each emission event. Emit per-artifact metrics to our telemetry bus and push scrubbed sample payloads to a redaction audit topic for privacy audits. Provide a compatibility shim that exposes a short-lived chunk_id that maps to artifact_id for older SDKs.
design_decisions: Use UUIDv4 for artifact_id to avoid collisions across nodes and restarts
Prefer attaching trace_link as a pair: trace_id and span_id in headers rather than encoding content in logs
Redaction is performed at the earliest possible stage (pre-logging) using the streaming scrubber service; raw content is never persisted in plain text
Metrics emitted are aggregated at the edge for cost control; full-resolution events are optionally sampled to the audit topic
Compatibility shim will map chunk_id -> artifact_id for 30 days and will surface a deprecation warning header
metric_definitions: stream.artifact.latency_ms: histogram (labels: artifact_id, model, route, tenant)
span_contract: When tracing is enabled the emitter attaches headers: x-rw-trace-id, x-rw-span-id, x-rw-artifact-id
A new child span is created for long-running artifact generation (>250ms) with span.kind='producer'
Span attributes must not contain raw token payloads; only metadata (token_count, model, prompt_hash) is allowed
Traces referencing artifact_id must include a 'stream.fragment' tag for downstream correlation
redaction_policy_summary: Streaming scrubber applies layered redaction: 1) deterministic PII patterns (emails, SSNs) masked, 2) user-defined prompt filters applied, 3) fallback entropy-based token suppression for high-risk outputs. Logs and span attributes use scrubbed payloads; raw payloads are routed to an encrypted audit topic with access controls and TTL=30d.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): instrument runtime in canary region with artifact_id + trace headers, sample 0.1% of payloads to audit topic
Phase 2: enable per-chunk metric emission and edge aggregation in us-east-1, observe cost and cardinality for 72h
Phase 3: enable compatibility shim for legacy SDKs and expose deprecation header to older clients
Phase 4: global rollout with migration doc and SDK updates; monitor error budget and SLOs
QA_checks: Unit tests for artifact_id generation and mapping table TTL
Integration tests verifying headers and per-chunk metrics arrive in test telemetry pipeline
Replay test ensuring scrubbed payloads are never present in standard logs
Load test to assert <2% latency regression at 99th percentile under typical batching profiles
